This guide is original writing, grounded in the public, open-source ATAK-CIV codebase. The code snippets are taken from (or trimmed from) the open-source helloworld example plugin and are reproduced here for instructional purposes.

Primary source

  • TAK-Product-Center/atak-civ — U.S. Government / TAK Product Center, open source, active https://github.com/TAK-Product-Center/atak-civ
    • Code referenced here is from release tag **5.5.1.10** (current line 5.5.x). Note main is an older 4.6.x baseline — the current code lives on the per-release upstream/5.5.x branches and matching tags.
    • README.md, BUILDING.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, LICENSE.md, THIRDPARTY.md
    • pluginsdk.zip (the ATAK Plugin SDK + atak-gradle-takdev 3.x)
    • plugin-examples/helloworld — the skeleton/example used throughout:
      • app/build.gradle — ATAK_VERSION 5.6.0, compileSdk 36, Java 17, flavors civ/mil/gov
      • app/src/main/assets/plugin.xml — single gov.tak.api.plugin.IPlugin extension
      • app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml
      • …/plugin/HelloWorldLifecycle.java — extends AbstractPlugin, IServiceController
      • …/plugin/HelloWorldTool.java — extends AbstractPluginTool
      • HelloWorldMapComponent.java, HelloWorldDropDownReceiver.java, sender/HelloWorldContactSender.java
    • plugin-examples/plugintemplate — minimal starting template
    • plugin-examples/plugintemplate-compose — Kotlin + Jetpack Compose template; source of the Kotlin & Compose page:
      • app/build.gradle — org.jetbrains.kotlin.android + …kotlin.plugin.compose, buildFeatures.compose, Compose BOM
      • …/PluginTemplateDropDownReceiver.kt — Kotlin/Compose UI receiver (+ the ComposeContext two-context wrapper)
      • …/plugin/PluginTemplateLifecycle.java, PluginTemplateTool.java (Java plumbing)
  • Superseded: deptofdefense/AndroidTacticalAssaultKit-CIV — archived read-only (May 2025); targeted ATAK 4.6 with the older transapps Lifecycle + ToolDescriptor plugin model.

Concepts referenced (public)

  • Cursor-on-Target (CoT) — the TAK event format; takproto (open source) documents the wire protocol: https://github.com/deptofdefense/AndroidTacticalAssaultKit-CIV (takproto/) and https://takproto.readthedocs.io.
  • MIL-STD-2525 / CoT type codes — marker affiliation/type scheme (e.g. a-f-G-U-C).

Licensing & attribution notes

  • ATAK-CIV is released as open source by the U.S. DoD and is EAR99 under the EAR. Work by U.S. Federal employees is generally public domain in the U.S.; elsewhere it is licensed per the repo's LICENSE.md.
  • ⚠️ Preserve vendor markings. Several example source files carry a PAR Government Systems "Unlimited Rights" copyright header. Those legends state that any reproduction of the software (or portions) must reproduce the markings. If you copy example source into your own project, keep the original headers.
  • Always consult **THIRDPARTY.md** for the licenses of bundled dependencies before redistributing anything that includes them.

ATAK API deep-dive pages (12–15)

The deep-dive API pages — Map items & graphics, Map events, CoT in depth, and Advanced & practical APIs — adapt the civilian topics under tak.gov's ATAK Developer Guide (Creating Graphics, Map Event Handling, Custom CoT Details, Listening to / Sending CoT, Import API, IO Abstraction Layer, Radial Menu API, Map Projections, Spinners, Working with Native Code, etc.) into original prose. Every class/method was cross-checked against the open-source helloworld example where it appears there; where the open-source code and the docs differ (e.g. getRootGroup() vs getRootMapGroup()), the open-source form is used and the difference noted. No TAK-MIL content is reproduced.

Out of scope (intentionally not covered)

This guide deliberately excludes anything that is not publicly redistributable: the gated tak.gov developer documentation, the Military SDK / TAK-MIL, interface control documents, and the keyed / Foreign-Military-Sales distribution pipeline. For those, go through tak.gov with appropriate government sponsorship — see TAK.gov's "Our Process" page for distribution, licensing, and export policy.
